source.title: Unveiling Invariances via Neural Network Pruning
source.authors: D. Xu; Yi-Zhou Sun; Wei Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no material truncation or garbling apparent.
record.tranche_reason: It compares a pruned, invariance-trained MLP derived from a fully connected supernetwork with a CNN on the same image datasets, using a different training recipe from the version's standard-training comparison.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports test-set performance for IUNET (MLPVIS) and an equivalent CNN. Other pruning and invariance results do not measure the claim versions' named behaviors and are not included.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out image-classification accuracy of dense MLPs, learned sparse MLP subnetworks, and CNNs. These results bear on V3, including its prediction that learning sparse local connections narrows the architecture gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the relevant vision conclusion: IUNET narrows the gap between deep MLPs and CNNs, while the corresponding CNN still outperforms IUNET-pruned MLPVIS. The authors also conclude that their framework improves ResNet and tabular MLP performance.
record.recipe_differences: The MLP is trained with the ILO objective, pruned by magnitude, lottery-ticket reinitialized, and finetuned; the comparison is against an equivalent CNN. This is not a controlled standard-training comparison of dense fully connected and convolutional networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the size of the reported accuracy difference.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruned subnetworks have greater prediction consistency under specified invariant transformations, including before training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Invariance-directed pruning can encode transformation consistency into network architectures.

record.problems: The architecture comparison uses an ILO-trained, pruned MLP and does not isolate architecture under a shared standard-training recipe. Reported values are accuracy, not training error or the train-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure a behavior named by the claim versions. The remaining pruning, invariance-consistency, and weight-visualization findings concern other outcomes or mechanisms.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.

A controlled isolation of local connectivity's contribution, and initialization of a fully connected network from a trained CNN. The sparse-network comparison changes initialization, objective, and pruning together.
Controlled comparisons of adaptive optimizers against SGD under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Held-out performance with versus without dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Dense MLPVIS test accuracies are 59.266 ± 0.050 on CIFAR-10, 31.052 ± 0.371 on CIFAR-100, and 84.463 ± 0.393 on SVHN. Add comparisons with the corresponding CNN and pruned MLP to capture both the ordinary architecture advantage and its reduction after pruning.

The authors report that IUNET learns more locally connected structures, supported by weight visualizations across the three vision datasets. This bears on the learned-local-connectivity clause, although it does not causally isolate locality from the other recipe changes.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V3. Reported uncertainties are standard deviations across three runs. Table 4 appears to repeat the ResNet IUNET values under an MLPVIS heading; Tables 1 and 2 agree on the values used in R1–R3.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
A width sweep past the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.

The study does not compare ordinary fully connected and convolutional networks trained from scratch with the same standard recipe, isolate local connectivity as the cause, or test learned sparse local connections and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under controlled tuning.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
The effect of adding dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN; corresponding CNN versus dense and IUNET-pruned MLPVIS
relationships.reason: R1–R3 show higher CNN accuracy throughout. The missing dense baselines in Table 1 also show that IUNET narrows the CNN advantage: from 16.584 to 11.003, 10.582 to 8.874, and 7.429 to 2.535 percentage points, respectively. Gap-reduction evidence is based on the text and tables.
relationships.display_finding: CNN accuracy remained higher than pruned MLPVIS accuracy, but the gap was smaller than for dense MLPVIS on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN. The comparison does not establish that locality caused the improvement.
